caption: S rotates |1> by 90 degrees, T by 45 degrees — distance from the origin never moves.

steps.label: S² = Z, T² = S, T⁴ = Z, T⁸ = I
steps.sub: Each verified by direct complex matrix multiplication

steps.label: Z is a "half-turn" (2 applications return to I)
steps.sub: S is a "quarter-turn" (4 applications); T an "eighth-turn" (8)

steps.label: Alone on a basis state, S and T do nothing measurable
steps.sub: They move the amplitude's angle, not its distance from the origin

steps.label: Their effect appears only once combined with H
steps.sub: A phase gate changes the relative angle an interference step depends on

steps.label: T is the finest-grained phase step of the three
steps.sub: 8 applications bring |1⟩'s phase all the way around the unit circle

steps.label: H + T (+ CNOT) approximate any single-qubit rotation
steps.sub: Repeated T rotations can land arbitrarily close to any angle

steps.label: Chapter 4's universal gate sets depend on this
steps.sub: A small, fixed toolkit that still reaches every possible rotation

steps.label: Phase gates are never used alone in a real circuit
steps.sub: They're always set up to feed a later interference step

subtitle: A continuous parameter θ — and the fixed gates you already know, hiding inside it.
